review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. CDFG and FishBase sources support shallow bay/harbor habitat and broad temperature tolerance; the SST band is a modelled estimate, not a measured preference.

profile.size: Min limit 14 inches TL / Bag limit 5 per harvester / day

profile.behavior: Navigates West Coast kelp forests, rocky reefs, and coastal upwelling zones.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for spotted sand bass.
factors.value_notes: FishBase reports broad tolerance from about 7.5-32 °C and a model-derived preferred-temperature estimate of 18.1-26.8 °C (mean 22.3 °C, 42 cells). CDFG describes southern California bay/lagoon habitats as warm-water refuges for this subtropical species. These support broad thermal relevance, but the preference estimate is model-derived rather than field-validated and does not establish the configured 15-24 °C / 17-22 °C band as a catch-probability curve.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for spotted sand bass.
factors.value_notes: CDFG describes southern California populations as restricted mainly to shallow sandy/muddy bays, harbors and coastal lagoons with eelgrass, surfgrass and rock relief. FishBase reports occurrence from 1-61 m, usually near sand/mud, rocks and eelgrass. This supports shallow habitat but not a universal 1-20 m / 3-15 m depth-preference curve; localized bay populations and warm-water refuges are important.
